subject: GPU onramp: staggered tranches & spot-fallback options
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@auricore.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion — high-level asks

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the chat yesterday. To move toward an internal signoff I need a concrete set of dedicated reservation options we can present to procurement and our infra team. High level:
- Target launch: mid-Jan 2027 (production beta) with gradual traffic ramp through Q2.
- Current inference footprint: peak ~220 concurrent RT requests, avg token generation ~120 tokens/request, typical seq len 512.
- SLO: p99 generation latency <= 900ms; cost sensitive — want to minimize committed spend while avoiding throttling.

Can you lay out 2–3 proposal structures that include: minimum committed GPUs (floor), staged ramp schedule (weeks), warmup/activation plan, and a fallback policy if capacity is constrained (prefer spot/preemptibles vs. queueing). Also please include what warm-start credits look like and a tentative timeline for provisioning.

If possible, attach a simple worksheet with scenario tiers so our procurement can see the delta between a conservative vs. aggressive commitment.

Priya and I are looping procurement on follow-ups.

Thanks — Sanjay

--
Sanjay Rao
Head of ML Infrastructure, Auricore
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@auricore.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@auricore.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: GPU onramp: staggered tranches & spot-fallback options

Sanjay — appreciate the detail. Attached is a concise proposal and a worksheet we can tailor. High-level options below (summary for procurement):

Option A — Conservative floor + gradual tranches- Minimum committed floor: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved).
- Stages: Week 0 activation (12 GPUs) -> Week 4 expand to 24 GPUs -> Week 10 expand to 40 GPUs (if traffic validated).
- Warmup: 2 weeks of warm-start credits (lower cost on initial traffic; KV-cache prepopulation assistance).
- Fallback: Preferred: allow spot-backed bursting up to 2x (subject to availability); Secondary: auto-queue with soft 95% traffic pass-through.

Option B — Accelerated onramp (risk-tolerant)- Minimum committed floor: 24 GPUs.
- Stages: Week 0 activation -> Week 2 expand to 48 GPUs -> Week 8 to steady-state (64 GPUs) if adoption shows.
- Warmup: 4 weeks of pre-provisioning + prioritized provisioning window.
- Fallback: Dedicated hot-standby reserved for critical endpoints; spot fallback only for non-latency-critical batch jobs.

Option C — Tranche-based rolling commits (cost-smoothing)- Commit tranches: 8 / 8 / 16 GPUs over three contract tranches (quarterly triggers).
- Activation: Each tranche has a 7–10 day activation window; total ramp planned across 10–12 weeks.
- Warmup: KV-cache seeding per tranche; adaptive batching tuned after each tranche.
- Fallback: Queue + progressive degradation with model variant fallbacks (lower-precision quant) to preserve SLA.

Engineering notes: our runtime supports incremental lane activation and KV cache prepopulation; we can schedule a warm-start maintenance window to minimize cold-starts for the initial tranche. I'll attach a worksheet with estimated token burn and cost deltas for each option.

Next steps: if you like one of these, we can convert the preferred path into a formal offer and include activation milestones and a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Best,
Lukas

--
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Adding the commercial lens — quick clarifications and a recommended starting structure for procurement to expedite: 

- Pilot offer (risk-limited): 8-week pilot with 8 reserved GPUs, including 2 weeks of warm-start credits and a one-time migration assistance day. Pilot pricing: reduced rate for first 8 weeks; converts to committed pricing if they elect to onboard within 30 days after pilot.
- Recommended default floor for enterprise SLAs: 16 GPUs. That floor keeps p99 headroom for their stated workload and allows safe bursting.
- If Auricore prefers tranches (Option C), set tranche triggers to business KPIs (daily API calls, error rate, cost per 1k tokens) so we can automate expansions.

I'll run numbers into the worksheet and share a PDF offer. Ben — can you include a quick note on activation lead times for US west regions and any constraints around preemptible bursts?

Thanks — Marissa

Attaching the scenario worksheet (auricore-gpu-worksheet-v3.csv) and a draft offer (auricore-draft-offer-v2.pdf). Key operational constraints to flag: 

- Provisioning lead time (US-west region): standard activation 7–10 business days for reserved lanes; accelerated 48–72 hours only for lanes with pre-approved capacity windows.
- Spot/backfill: we can route non-critical burst traffic to spot instances up to 150% of reserved capacity, but preemptions may occur. For their p99 SLA critical endpoints, we recommend hot-standby reserved or model-fall back routes (quantized variant).
- Minimum commitment redline: to keep predictable costs under our SLA-backed offering, we should ask procurement to accept a 12-GPU minimum floor for contract conversion after pilot.

Requested action items: 
1) Sanjay/Priya — pick preferred option (A/B/C or Pilot).
2) If Option C (tranches), confirm tranche cadence (30/60/90 days).
3) Marissa/Legal to prepare a short-form amendment if they want accelerated 48–72h activation windows.

DocuSign: we will generate an envelope once Auricore confirms the option. Also adding a SOC2 evidence checklist separately (auricore-soc2-evidence-request.xlsx).

--

Team — thanks for the rapid follow-up and the worksheet. Auricore's procurement prefers the tranche-based approach (Option C) with the following clarifications before we sign: 
- Tranche cadence: 30 / 60 / 90 days (activate 8 / 8 / 16 GPUs respectively).
- Warm-start: please commit to KV-cache seeding for each tranche and one coordinated maintenance window per tranche to complete prepopulation.
- Fallback: we accept queueing + quantized model variant fallback for 10% of traffic, but critical endpoints must have access to reserved hot-standby during business hours.
- Piloting: waive the pilot-to-contract conversion fee if conversion happens within 45 days.

Can you update the draft offer to reflect the tranche cadence and the warm-start commitments and send the DocuSign envelope? Also, SOC2 artifact request has been submitted — procurement will expect those links alongside the contract.

Confirmed next step: Marissa/Ben — update PDF and create DocuSign, Lukas/Karthik — confirm warm-start windows and activation runbook.
